collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DISABILITY AND HUMAN DIVERSITY (DIV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Disabled villagers, chronic illness and every kind of body, skin, hair and face: wheelchairs with real wheels, crutches, canes, ear trumpets, signs and lenses made from island materials; good days and hard days; competence, humor and opinions. Sometimes the difference is the story. Often it's just part of the scenery.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A new workmate thinks a villager who avoids their eyes and names the weather dislikes them: ask straight out, or ask a friend.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) doesn't look people in the eye. It feels too much, like staring into the sun. (subject.He/she) looks at their shoulder, or the ground, or a tree just behind them. (subject.He/she) also always says hello the same way: by telling them the exact weather. "Good morning. Clouds from the east. Rain by midday." (friend) is new to working with (subject.him/her), and has decided (subject) must not like (friend.him/her).

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: "Have I done something?" asks (friend). (subject) looks at (friend.his/her) left ear, puzzled. "No. Why?" (friend) explains. (subject) thinks about it. "I don't look at anyone's eyes. And I tell everyone the weather. It's how I say I'm glad to see them." (friend) laughs with relief. The next morning (friend.he/she) gets: "Good morning. Clear. Hot later." (friend.He/she) decides it's the nicest greeting on Isola.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) asks (old_friend), an old friend of (subject)'s, who laughs. "That's just how (subject.he/she) is. If (subject.he/she) tells you the weather, (subject.he/she) likes you. If (subject.he/she) tells you the weather AND the tide, (subject.he/she) REALLY likes you." For weeks, (friend) waits. Then one morning: "Clouds from the north. Low tide at noon." (friend) is ridiculously pleased all day.
